item.title: Knee — Active Soft-Tissue Release
clinicalUse: Use when assessment identifies a relevant impairment in Knee and the parent technique fits the patient's presentation.
Primary treatment target: knee flexion/extension, patellofemoral/tibiofemoral symptoms and functional loading.
Retain the technique only if it produces a meaningful within-session improvement.
patientPosition: Supine, prone or sitting with the knee supported in the position required by the technique.
therapistPosition: Stand beside the knee with hands close to the joint line and the limb fully supported.
stabilization: Stabilize femur, tibia or patella depending on the target.
contact: Use broad contact and avoid sustained compression over the fibular head/common peroneal nerve.
Establish a tolerable contact over the target muscle/tendon while it is relatively shortened.
Maintain contact as the patient actively lengthens or moves the tissue.
forceDirection: Pressure remains controlled while the patient produces the movement; avoid dragging aggressively across skin.
dosage: Often 3–8 slow active repetitions followed by reassessment and loading.
steps: 1. Record the exact comparable sign for Knee: knee flexion/extension, patellofemoral/tibiofemoral symptoms and functional loading.
2. Screen regional red flags, contraindications and technique-specific precautions before touching the patient.
3. Position and stabilize the patient so the target is comfortable and the manual input can be localized.
4. Apply a low-force trial using the parent technique principles and the region-specific contact described above.
5. Monitor pain quality, symptom distribution, guarding and patient confidence throughout.
6. Re-test the original comparable sign immediately after the trial.
7. Keep the technique only when the response is useful, then transfer the gain into active movement, loading or self-management.
mistakes: Applying the technique because it is familiar rather than because the examination supports it.
Using more force when the response is unclear or worsening.
Failing to re-test the exact movement or function that justified the treatment.
safety: Avoid routine manual therapy with suspected DVT, fracture, acute instability, infection or uncleared postoperative restriction.
Stop or modify if symptoms peripheralize, neurological status worsens, the response is disproportionate or the patient asks to stop.
item.visualCue: Knee assessment → correct regional setup → Active Soft-Tissue Release → immediate comparable-sign re-test.

subTechniques.name: Quadriceps — Active Soft-Tissue Release
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve pain, movement tolerance or tissue-related function when this target is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine, prone or sitting with the knee comfortably supported.
subTechniques.contact: Tolerable contact over Quadriceps while the tissue begins in a shortened position.
subTechniques.direction: Maintain controlled contact while the patient actively lengthens/moves the target tissue.
subTechniques.dosage: Often 3–8 slow repetitions followed by reassessment.
subTechniques.reassess: Re-test the region's original pain, range or functional task.
